name: Kerala: Backwaters and Kochi
tagline: A green, laid-back coast of palm-fringed backwaters, spice hills, old Portuguese and Dutch trading quarters and one of India's best regional cuisines.
highlight: A dawn canoe ride on a quiet backwater canal, with kingfishers on the palms and village life waking up.
shortDescription: Kerala's slow, watery landscapes: houseboats and canoes on the Alleppey backwaters, the historic port of Fort Kochi, the tea hills of Munnar and a rich food and dance heritage.
metaDescription: A Kerala travel guide: the Alleppey backwaters and houseboats, Fort Kochi, Chinese fishing nets, Kathakali, Munnar tea hills, Kerala food, Ayurveda, when to go and a four-day plan.
nearestAirport: Cochin International (COK), about 45 minutes from Kochi
knownFor: Backwaters, houseboats, Fort Kochi, tea hills, Ayurveda, seafood
goodFor: Relaxing, nature, food, culture, a gentler India

image.alt: A traditional houseboat on the palm-lined backwaters near Alleppey in Kerala

intro: Kerala is a narrow strip of land on India's south-western coast, between the Arabian Sea and the Western Ghats. Its long trading history brought Arab, Chinese, Portuguese, Dutch, British and Jewish merchants to its ports, and the mix of influences shows in its architecture, food and religion. Hindus, Muslims and Christians live side by side, and the state has some of the highest literacy and health indicators in India.

The backwaters, a network of lagoons, canals and rivers running behind the coast for hundreds of kilometres, are the region's signature. Around Alleppey (Alappuzha) and Kumarakom, villages, rice paddies and coconut groves line the water, and life moves by boat. A night on a traditional houseboat, or a day in a canoe, is the standard way to experience it.

Kochi (Cochin) is the gateway. Its old quarter, Fort Kochi, has Portuguese and Dutch buildings, a 16th-century synagogue, art galleries and the famous cantilevered Chinese fishing nets. In the hills inland, Munnar's tea plantations offer cool air and views. Kerala is the easiest and calmest part of India for a first visit, and a natural counterpart to the north.

whyVisit.intro: Kerala offers a slower, greener India, with excellent food and easy travel.

points.title: The backwaters
points.text: A maze of canals and lagoons, best seen from a small boat or a canoe.

points.title: Fort Kochi
points.text: Colonial buildings, galleries and cafés in an atmospheric old port.

points.title: Tea hills and spices
points.text: Munnar's rolling plantations and the spice gardens near Thekkady.

points.title: Superb food
points.text: Coconut-based curries, fresh seafood, appam and banana-leaf meals.

points.title: Living traditions
points.text: Kathakali dance-drama, temple festivals and Ayurvedic treatment.

attractionsIntro: A typical trip runs from Kochi to the backwaters, with an optional detour to the hills.

attractions.name: The Alleppey backwaters
attractions.text: The heart of the backwater region, with canals and lagoons around Alleppey and the huge Vembanad Lake. Houseboats, shared ferries and canoes all travel through them.
attractions.tip: Choose a small canal in the early morning, when it is calm.

attractions.name: The Chinese fishing nets, Fort Kochi

image.file: File:Sunset with Chinese Fishing Nets, Fort Kochi 2.jpg
image.alt: Chinese fishing nets silhouetted at sunset in Fort Kochi

attractions.text: Huge cantilevered nets, lowered into the water by teams of fishermen, along the waterfront at Fort Kochi. They are traditionally linked to Chinese traders, and are best at sunset.
attractions.tip: Buy fresh fish and have it cooked nearby.

attractions.name: Jew Town and the Paradesi Synagogue
attractions.text: A quarter of antique shops and spice warehouses in Mattancherry, with a synagogue dating from 1568, one of the oldest in the Commonwealth, decorated with blue Chinese tiles.
attractions.tip: Check opening days, as it is closed on Saturdays.

attractions.name: Mattancherry Palace and St. Francis Church
attractions.text: A Portuguese-built palace with Kerala murals, and one of the oldest European churches in India, where Vasco da Gama was first buried in 1524.
attractions.tip: See both in the same morning.

attractions.name: Munnar tea plantations

image.alt: Rolling green tea plantations in the hills around Munnar

attractions.text: A hill station at about 1,500 metres in the Western Ghats, surrounded by tea estates, waterfalls and viewpoints. It is about 4 hours by road from Kochi.

thingsToDoIntro: Kerala is for slowing down, and for time on and beside the water.

thingsToDo.title: Stay on a houseboat
thingsToDo.text: A converted kettuvallam, a traditional rice barge, with a crew and cook, drifts through the backwaters.
thingsToDo.tip: Choose a licensed boat and check the type of fuel and waste practices.

thingsToDo.title: Take a canoe trip
thingsToDo.text: A small boat can reach narrow canals that big houseboats cannot, past homes, rice fields and temples.

thingsToDo.title: Watch a Kathakali performance
thingsToDo.text: A traditional dance-drama with elaborate make-up and costumes, based on epics.
thingsToDo.tip: Arrive early to watch the make-up.

thingsToDo.title: Try an Ayurvedic massage
thingsToDo.text: Kerala is a centre for Ayurveda, with treatments from short massages to multi-week programmes.

thingsToDo.title: Visit a spice plantation
thingsToDo.text: See pepper, cardamom, cinnamon and vanilla growing, near Thekkady and Munnar.

thingsToDo.title: Take a ferry
thingsToDo.text: A public ferry from Alleppey to Kottayam offers a cheap backwater trip of a few hours.

foodIntro: Kerala's cuisine relies on coconut, curry leaves, pepper, seafood and rice, and it is one of the best in India.

foods.name: Appam and stew
foods.text: A lacy rice-flour pancake with a soft centre, eaten with a mild coconut milk stew of vegetables or chicken.

foods.name: Kerala fish curry
foods.text: Fish cooked in a sour, spicy sauce with coconut milk and kokum, often in a clay pot.

foods.name: Sadya
foods.text: A vegetarian feast served on a banana leaf, with more than 20 dishes, at festivals such as Onam.

foods.name: Karimeen pollichathu
foods.text: Pearl spot fish marinated in spices, wrapped in banana leaf and grilled.

foods.name: Puttu and kadala curry
foods.text: Steamed cylinders of rice flour and coconut with a black chickpea curry.

foods.name: Toddy
foods.text: A mild palm sap alcohol, sold in licensed toddy shops with spicy food.

accommodation.intro: Stay in Fort Kochi for its atmosphere, and choose a houseboat or a homestay for the backwaters.

areas.name: Fort Kochi
areas.text: Restored colonial houses and small hotels.

areas.name: Alleppey and Kumarakom
areas.text: Houseboats, resorts and homestays by the water.

gettingThere.intro: Kochi is the main gateway to Kerala, with an international airport and rail links.

options.text: Direct flights from Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and some Gulf and international cities.
options.detail: The airport is about 45 minutes from Fort Kochi.

options.text: Long-distance trains reach Ernakulam Junction from Mumbai, Bengaluru and Chennai.
About 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours from Kochi by car or bus.

gettingAround.intro: Kerala's compact size makes it easy to move between the main places by road, train or boat.

options.text: The easiest way to link Kochi, Alleppey and Munnar.

options.detail: Buses are cheap, and trains are comfortable.

options.text: Public ferries in Kochi and on the backwaters.

bestTime.headline: October–March
bestTime.summary: Kerala is tropical, with a strong monsoon from June to September.

seasons.text: Warm, dry and pleasant. Peak season.
Hot and humid, cooler in the hills.
Heavy rain, lush landscapes and cheaper rates. Popular for Ayurveda.

bestTime.avoid: The heaviest monsoon weeks in July if you want to be outdoors.

itinerary.title: Four days in Kerala
itinerary.intro: Kochi's heritage first, then the backwaters, and a rest.

days.title: Fort Kochi
days.afternoon: Jew Town, Mattancherry and St. Francis Church.
days.evening: The Chinese fishing nets and a Kathakali show.

days.title: Dawn on the canals
days.evening: A rest, or a beach at Marari.

days.title: Munnar or return
days.morning: Drive to Munnar, or return to Kochi.
days.evening: Depart or stay in the hills.

tipsIntro: A few things help you enjoy Kerala.
tips: Choose a small houseboat, or a canoe, for a quieter experience.
Check that a houseboat is licensed, and ask about waste disposal.
Carry insect repellent for the evenings on the water.
Try a banana-leaf meal at a local restaurant.
Dress modestly at temples, and ask before entering.
Carry a rain jacket, even outside the monsoon.
Book Munnar accommodation in advance in high season.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Kerala?
faq.a: Four days for Kochi and the backwaters, and six or seven if you add Munnar and the beaches.
For one night, yes, for the experience. Big, crowded houseboats can be less pleasant than small boats or canoes.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Kerala?
faq.a: October to March. The monsoon is wet but green, and popular for Ayurveda.
It is considered one of the safest and calmest parts of India.
No. Seafood, chicken and beef are all eaten, though there are excellent vegetarian dishes.

faq.q: Do I need to worry about the monsoon?
faq.a: It brings heavy rain and some travel disruption, but many visitors enjoy the green landscapes and quiet.
